who_it_covers: Any business using a chatbot with Maine customers
what_it_requires: If a customer could reasonably think they are talking to a real person, you must tell them clearly that it is a bot.
enforcement: Counts as a violation of the Maine Unfair Trade Practices Act

who_it_covers: Businesses using generative AI with Utah consumers; licensed professions
what_it_requires: If a customer clearly asks whether they are talking to AI, you must tell them. Licensed professionals (for example in health or finance) must say it up front in "high-risk" conversations.
enforcement: Utah Division of Consumer Protection; fines up to $5,000 per violation of an order

who_it_covers: Makers of mental health chatbots used by Utah residents
what_it_requires: Must disclose the bot is AI and limits how they use or sell users' personal information and ads.

law: General Business Law Art. 47 (budget bill S 3008, ch. 58 of 2025)
what_it_requires: Must have a plan to spot users who talk about suicide or self-harm and refer them to crisis help. Must remind users at the start and at least every 3 hours that they are not talking to a human.
enforcement: New York Attorney General; up to $15,000 per day

who_it_covers: Anyone offering therapy or mental health services in Illinois
what_it_requires: AI can't provide therapy or make therapy decisions. Licensed providers can still use AI for admin work like scheduling and notes.
enforcement: Illinois Department of Financial and Professional Regulation; up to $10,000 per violation

who_it_covers: Makers of AI systems and mental health providers in Nevada
what_it_requires: AI can't be offered as if it provides professional mental or behavioral health care. Providers can use it for admin support.
enforcement: Civil penalty up to $15,000 per violation

what_it_requires: Must tell users the bot is not human, have a suicide and self-harm plan, and add extra protections for minors. Yearly reports to the state start July 1, 2027. Bots used only for customer service are not covered.
Must disclose the bot is AI when a person could be misled, remind minors every hour, have suicide-prevention steps and not pose as mental health care. Yearly reports start Jan 1, 2028.
enforcement: Treated as an unfair or deceptive practice; no private lawsuits

who_it_covers: Only "large" businesses: over $500 million a year in revenue
what_it_requires: Can't pass off a customer service bot as a human. During business hours, customers must be able to ask for a real person and get one within 15 minutes (or an appointment within 1 business day). Hold times are capped.
enforcement: Public prosecutors only; $5,000 for a first violation, $10,000 after that

what_it_requires: Must do child-safety risk checks and get independent audits.
Bans making or selling toys with a built-in companion chatbot for now.
starts: Jan 1, 2027 (California's default start date); ban runs until Jan 1, 2031

what_it_requires: Must disclose the service is AI, protect minors, have a suicide plan and not pose as a licensed professional. Bots used for customer support or buying and selling are not covered.
Disclosure and safety rules for companion bots. Customer service bots are not covered.
enforcement: People harmed can sue for actual damages or $1,000 per violation, whichever is more

what_it_requires: Required safety features, including crisis steps. Customer service bots are not covered.
enforcement: Rhode Island Attorney General; up to $15,000 per day

what_it_requires: Disclosure and safety rules, with extra rules for minors. Customer service bots that don't build an ongoing relationship are not covered.
enforcement: Violation of the Consumer Protection Act

what_it_requires: Must tell users it's AI at the start and every 3 hours (every hour for minors). Customer service bots are not covered.
enforcement: Georgia Attorney General; up to $10,000 per knowing violation

what_it_requires: Disclosure, protections for minors and a suicide plan. Bots a business uses to help its customers, and internal-only tools, are not covered.
enforcement: Iowa Attorney General; $1,000 per violation, up to $500,000

what_it_requires: Disclosure, protections for minors and a suicide plan. Customer service bots are not covered.
enforcement: Idaho Attorney General; $1,000 per violation, up to $500,000

what_it_requires: Disclosure, protections for minors and a suicide plan. A business's customer service bot is not covered.
enforcement: Nebraska Attorney General; no private lawsuits
